subject: Draft MAP: POC environment dependencies & owners — next steps
messages:
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: santiago.ruiz@brightwave.com, chris.nolan@brightwave.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, anna.lee@brightwave.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MAP: POC environment dependencies & owners — next steps

Hi Santiago / Chris —

Thanks again for the call today. I recorded the decisions and open items into the attached Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft; the file includes milestone owners and a proposed timeline. High-level recap + immediate asks below so we can lock the POC start window.

Quick recap (POC goal): Validate Redwood inference integration for BrightWave’s recommendation pipeline on a small corpus (2k daily queries) with latency SLOs ~120ms p50.

Key POC environment milestones (owners in parentheses):
- VPC peering / routing validation (BrightWave Network / Anna) — BrightWave to open peering request and provide VPC CIDRs.
- IP allowlists & firewall rules (BrightWave SRE / devops@brightwave.com & Redwood net team) — need allowed source IP ranges for our egress + a small canary range for testing.
- SSO / SAML integration (BrightWave IdP / Karthik) — we support SP-initiated SAML; please confirm required attributes (email/nameid).
- Secrets & KMS (BrightWave Security / Redwood) — option to BYO AWS KMS CMK or use Redwood-managed key; we need KMS ARN if BYO.

Target timeline: aim to start connectivity tests the week of Nov 30 and begin the POC the week of Dec 7. If anything blocks that, flag it now and we’ll adjust.

Immediate asks for the next 48 hours:
1) Anna / devops@brightwave.com — can you share your VPC CIDRs and a maintainer contact for peering?
2) Santiago / Chris — confirm whether you will BYO KMS (send ARN) or prefer Redwood-managed key.
3) BrightWave security — list SAML attributes required and the metadata endpoint (or a SAML metadata XML).

Attachments: Draft_MAP_BrightWave_v1.xlsx (Excel) — includes milestone table; brightwave_network_diagram.png (PNG).

I’ll follow up with a shorter milestone table seeded into HubSpot after we hear back. Thanks —

Laura Bennett
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: santiago.ruiz@brightwave.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: chris.nolan@brightwave.com, anna.lee@brightwave.com, devops@brightwave.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:05:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: POC environment dependencies & owners — next steps

Laura —

Appreciate the summary. Quick answers inline:
- VPC CIDRs: 10.24.0.0/16 (prod-like), 10.25.0.0/24 (POC). Anna (cc) is our network lead and will take the peering action.
- IP allowlist: we need the static IPs you'll use for egress so we can add firewall rules. Can you provide a list or an expected range?
- SAML: we prefer SP-initiated. Required attributes: email (emailAddress), givenName, familyName, and a custom tenant_id claim. Our IdP metadata URL: https://idp.brightwave.com/metadata.xml
- KMS: We prefer BYO AWS KMS; I’ll ask security for the ARN — will follow up by EOD.

Two small asks: can you provide a one-page connectivity checklist we can hand to our infra ops team, and a sample SP metadata from Redwood to help our IdP team?

—Santiago
Santiago Ruiz
Head of Platform | BrightWave Analytics
santiago.ruiz@brightwave.com

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: santiago.ruiz@brightwave.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, anna.lee@brightwave.com
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 16:00:35 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MAP: POC environment dependencies & owners — next steps

Thanks Santiago — tagging the short items you asked for.

1) Redwood static egress ranges (for IP allowlist):
- Canaries/test: 34.212.10.128/29
- POC traffic: 34.212.10.0/27
- Fallback/control plane: 34.212.11.0/24
(These are NATed egress ranges; we can provide exact IPs for the initial two canary nodes on request.)

2) SAML support: we support SP-initiated SAML with the following minimal attributes: NameID (transient or email), mail, givenName, sn (surname). For BrightWave’s custom tenant_id claim we can map an attribute as long as the IdP exposes it. I’ve attached a sample SP metadata file and a short one-page connectivity checklist for your ops team.

3) KMS options: if you BYO KMS we need the ARN and permission to create a grant for the Redwood service principal. If you prefer Redwood-managed keys, we’ll generate and manage keys on your behalf — both options are supported.

Attachments: redwood_poc_runbook_v0.3.pdf (PDF), redwood_sp_metadata.xml (XML)

I’ll also drop these into the HubSpot deal note. Laura — I recommend we mark the VPC peering and IP allowlist as blocking items for the Nov 30 canary.

-Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Perfect — thanks all. Confirming Redwood can do the Nov 30 connectivity check at 9:00am PT. I’ve updated the MAP milestone table (attached) with the following owners & blockers so we’re aligned:

Milestone summary (short):
- VPC peering request submitted (Owner: Anna Lee / BrightWave) — blocker until we receive peering acceptance.
- IP allowlist configured (Owner: BrightWave SRE + Redwood net) — blocker until we provide final canary IPs.
- SAML integration completed (Owner: BrightWave IdP + Karthik) — dependent on IdP metadata + attribute confirmation.
- KMS key available (Owner: BrightWave Security) — dependent on ARN or confirmation to use Redwood-managed key.

Next steps:
- Anna / devops: please confirm peering request target date (ideally by Nov 23).
- Santiago / security: send KMS ARN or confirm Redwood-managed key by EOD Nov 17.
- Anna / IdP: confirm metadata endpoint and required attributes (we have idp.brightwave.com/metadata.xml from Santiago).

I’ll create the HubSpot milestone task for the Nov 30 connectivity check and send an invite for the 9:00am PT slot. If any blocker surfaces, we’ll re-align the dates and I’ll update the MAP in HubSpot + the attached Excel.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.
